findings.title: Per-task cost silently drops stop-bounded task spans
findings.what: The public contract says taskCount contains one span per StopHook boundary plus a populated trailing span, but the implementation creates buckets only when a dated token entry maps to that index. Any stop interval with no mapped entry is omitted, so taskCount and the mean/median/p95 denominator no longer represent every declared task span.
findings.fix: Initialize a zero-cost bucket for every stop index before assigning entries, add the trailing bucket only when at least one valid entry falls after the final stop, and then aggregate all initialized boundary buckets.
findings.acceptance: Add an aggregatePerTaskCost test with two valid StopHook timestamps but token entries mapping only to the first interval; assert taskCount is 2, the missing interval contributes zero cost, and mean/median/p95 use both boundary spans. Add a second assertion that no trailing span is created without a post-final-stop entry.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that lines 356-358 explicitly define the denominator, while lines 405-416 populate taskCosts exclusively from Map keys created by token entries; the dispatched test file imports no aggregatePerTaskCost coverage.

findings.title: Per-task attribution performs an entries-by-stops linear scan
findings.what: Stop timestamps are sorted once, but every token entry calls Array.findIndex from the beginning. A session with E token entries and S stop events performs O(E×S) comparisons during ingest, producing avoidable latency for long-running sessions.
findings.fix: Replace findIndex with a lower-bound binary search over the sorted stop timestamps, or sort entries and advance a single monotonic stop pointer.
findings.acceptance: Add a large synthetic-session benchmark or comparison-count probe showing attribution scales O(E log S) or O(E+S), while asserting byte-identical task-cost results against a small reference implementation.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass confirmed stops are sorted at lines 391-394 but line 410 restarts a linear findIndex for every entry in the loop at lines 406-413; no cache, binary search, or monotonic cursor limits the repeated scan.
